chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: Red Onion Jazz Babies, Beatty and Todd, and trombonist Aaron Thompson
summary: They go through the 1924 session as Josephine Beatty with Louis, Bechet, Lil and Buster Bailey, and she recalls Aaron Thompson only faintly.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now, who wrote Nobody Knows the Way I Feel This Morning?
I remember recording it. But I don't remember --
And this is what you did with Clarence Todd -- no, Cakewalking Babies you did with Clarence Todd.
Now, this is when you were recording with the Red Onion Jazz Babies --
-- Louie and Sidney Bechet and Lil --
That's my sister, my baby sister.
Yeah, (inaudible) it was Beatty and Todd. And --
I have -- I don't have "Early Every Morn --"
Uh-huh. Who'd I record that with?
That was from the same session. But it's possible you didn't sing on it.
"Early Every Morn," yeah. That was Gennett (inaudible), that was when you were under contract to Paramount actually.
And I did that under my sister's name too or somebody else's name.
Yeah, your sister's name, and Everybody Loves My Baby and "Texas Moanin' Blues." Now, you did those here in New York in 1924.
And that was Jack Palmer -- (Songs) "Everybody Loves My Baby -- but my baby don't love nobody but me." I
Yeah. And Buster Bailey was playing soprano sax, Aaron Thompson, trombone.

Aaron Thompson -- he was -- I don't think Mr. Thompson was too -- I mean was too celebrated, but he was a good trombonist, and I don't remember -- I don't remember having seen him for years and years and years. I don't remember having seen him for -- well, I don't remember -- yes, I did see him a few times after I recorded, but I don't remember after that.
He's here in New York, though. He was here in New York.
Oh. Well, this is many years ago.
